headline: Statistical methods integrate chromatin and perturbation data at single-cell resolution
label: Single Cell Regulatory Genomics Methods
summary: New methods pair Perturb-seq, CUT&Tag, and scATAC-seq data with explicit causal, noise, or power models to resolve regulatory mechanisms.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational frameworks that pair sequencing modalities with explicit statistical models of noise, bias, or experimental design. CMAPS applies semiparametric causal mediation with adaptive bootstrap FDR control to infer mediators of CRISPR perturbation effects in Perturb-seq data, while PerturbPlan provides an analytical power formula for Perturb-seq and TAP-seq that reduces runtime relative to simulation. ATLAS integrates paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq through WNN graphs for multi-omic trajectory inference, and PATTY corrects Tn5 open-chromatin bias in bulk and single-cell CUT&Tag using paired ATAC-seq. HiCPotts models Hi-C noise with zero-inflated Negative Binomial terms. Experimental multimodal advances include icCITE-plex and DOGMA-plex, which profile RNA, protein, and chromatin responses to chemical screens. The shared element is integration of modalities with explicit modeling rather than a single shared dataset or method.
